_README: BOOTSTRAP ONTOLOGY — NOT the real one. Read this before using it for anything.
WHAT THIS IS: the minimum entity set needed to make seed-lint's Rule A and Rule B
executable and TESTED today. Every row is transcribed from a COMMITTED, CHECKABLE
source in this repo — docs/process/research-keyword-rigor.md (rev 3) SS4.2, whose
offender table names each synonym pair and the one parent/constituent pair, and SS6 V3
for the high-prior list. Nothing here is invented (CLAUDE.md rule 6).
WHAT THIS IS NOT: the Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I ontology. That is 621
single botanical drugs / 393 species / 323 genera / 115 families across 9 volumes
(1986-2016), it is legally canonical, free, and published — and per the research it is
the real backbone. It belongs in packages/ontology/ (fleet-level, hashed, human-signed)
and does NOT exist yet. This file covers 18 entities. It is a scaffold, not a substitute.
WHY AN ONTOLOGY GAP IS SAFE HERE: Rules A and B can only fire on entities they know.
An entity this file has never heard of would sail past both. That is precisely why
RULE C (provenance) is the actual guarantee: seeds = ontology UNION audience, nothing
else, so an unknown seed fails on provenance regardless of A and B. A and B are the
fast, legible failures that NAME the specific mistake; C is the backstop that catches
the modes nobody imagined. Do not mistake this file's coverage for the gate's coverage.
THE LOAD-BEARING DISTINCTION: synonyms[] means SAME REFERENT (amalaki IS amla) -> Rule A.
constituents[] means DIFFERENT REFERENT (curcumin is a chemical IN turmeric) -> Rule B.
Merging these two lists re-opens the exact hole that produced 'turmeric curcumin', and
Rule A alone waves it straight through. loadOntology() FAILS on any term appearing in
both lists of one entity.

entities._note: SS4.2: 'Curcumin is not a synonym of turmeric — it is a chemical constituent of it.' Verified live, different demand AND different CPC: turmeric 301,000/$0.86 vs curcumin 60,500/$2.48. The CPC gap is itself the signal that curcumin is a commercially distinct supplement-buyer query — a fact the concatenation destroyed. 'turmeric curcumin' = 27,100 is a supplement-LABEL artifact, not a topic.
entities._sanskrit_source: हल्दी is recorded in the SS5.2 live India/hi pull at 18,100/mo. Added after seed-lint CORRECTLY rejected the seed 'हल्दी' as unresolvable against an ontology that lacked it — the lint caught an ontology gap, which is precisely Rule C's job.

entities._note: A legitimate entity and a legitimate query IN ITS OWN RIGHT (60,500 US, CPC $2.48). 'curcumin' alone must PASS the lint. Only the welding of it to its parent is banned.

SS4.2: 'Passes bacopa monnieri (one binomial = one name).' The ontology deliberately lists BOTH the binomial and the bare genus 'bacopa' — so a naive two-forms-of-one-entity rule WOULD flag the legitimate binomial. Their spans overlap, so Rule A correctly passes it. This row exists to keep that precision honest.

High-prior (SS6 V3). 201,000 US — and it collides EXACTLY with 'ashwagandha benefits' at 201,000. SS6 V8 records that collision as the reason a 'duplicate volume => grouping artifact' rule was REJECTED: on a 47-value ladder, collisions are the pigeonhole principle, not evidence.

V4 CONTAMINATION EXEMPLAR — not a demand finding. India 1,500,000/mo at competition LOW; US Labs 12,100 at keyword_difficulty 0. A six-figure-adjacent abstract concept nobody competes for is definitionally contamination: 'Ojas' is a common Indian personal/brand name. Un-flagged it would have made 'concepts' the site's top cluster and driven the entire IA off a homonym.
